main_body: Timber-framed house with a large hipped tile roof, half-timbered front walls, and a gabled porch bay in front
top_band: At the middle column: dark-brown to mid-brown shingle roof slope with lighter tile highlights from row 0 to about row 44. It is a foreshortened slope, and the porch gable roof overlaps it at rows 35-45.
evidence: The roof is a large shingled slope above the walls and carries the top surface, which is what the contract asks for on a building. A dark eave line and shadow band sit at rows ~42-47 directly above the cream plaster and timber wall (rows 47-75). The porch has its own gable and a wall below it, down to row 106. The windows and doors have dark inner frames and read as inset. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The roof is well made: individual shingles, 4-5 brown steps, highlight scallops along the hips, and a brick chimney. The outline is a dark brown/maroon lean rather than neutral black. The plaster wall panels between the timbers are large areas of one flat cream with no speckle or grain, while the references have speckled plaster or shaded individual stones. The walls use only about 3 tones (cream, one shadow tone, dark timber), so the wall tiles are much sparser than the roof tiles and the reference wall tiles. The piece reads as slightly thinner and flatter than the reference, and the flat wall fills tip it to fail.
